payload.issue: scripts/emit-dashboard-row.sh:130 defaults telegram_sent="yes" unless the caller explicitly passes --telegram-sent no. Any dedup-SKIP cycle whose caller omits the flag gets a DASHBOARD.md row that permanently and falsely claims a Telegram alert was sent, when none was.

evidence.script_defect: scripts/emit-dashboard-row.sh line 130: local ... telegram_sent="yes" (default) ; line 146: --telegram-sent flag overrides it ; line 207: if telegram_sent=yes, appends ', WARN Telegram sent)' to the permanent DASHBOARD.md row

instance_1.notebook_cycle: c67 (dedup-SKIP against c66 ledger entry, per this session's own memory record)
instance_1.ground_truth: dedup-skip cycle, no BUG-channel alert should have fired

instance_2.notebook_cycle: c71 (this tick's spawn, dedup-SKIP against the same c66 ledger entry)
instance_2.ground_truth: agent's own [OUTPUT-CONTRACT] explicitly states telegram_sent=0, and its report prose states 'No BUG channel alert sent (dedup-gated)' -- directly contradicts the permanent DASHBOARD.md record written moments later

evidence.likely_correct_baseline: de7663377 / sys-20260806T171507-1243 / c66 -- the genuinely NEW (non-dedup) occurrence -- telegram_sent=yes is plausibly correct there since a real WARN alert would fire on first detection

payload.impact: DASHBOARD.md is meant to be a human-readable operational record; anyone reading it believes a human/on-call got paged for every dedup-skipped recurrence of this signal, when in fact only the first occurrence paged. Misleads incident-response expectations and could mask actual paging gaps on other checks that share this same script.
payload.requested_action: fix scripts/emit-dashboard-row.sh: either flip the default to telegram_sent="no" (safer default, matching the majority dedup-skip case) and require callers to explicitly pass --telegram-sent yes when a real alert fires, OR require all callers to explicitly pass the flag (fail loud if omitted). Also worth a broader sweep of DASHBOARD.md for other check_ids that may carry the same false claim from other callers of this script.
payload.occurrence_note: 2 confirmed instances this session (c67, c71), same script default, same false claim shape -- crosses recurring-bug 2+ threshold on first investigation. Not yet tracked in memory under any existing feedback file (new finding, not a re-litigation of an owned decision).
